headline: BMW unveils iX5 electric SUV with 435 miles range
summary: The iX5 60 xDrive EV offers impressive range and power, with a 140kWh battery and 570 horsepower. It starts at $79,800 and hits dealer lots by end of 2026.
details: The iX5 60 xDrive is fitted with a huge 140kWh battery and puts out 570 horsepower. BMW has unveiled its new X5 lineup, and for the first time, there's a fully electric version among the many powertrain options.
The iX5 60 xDrive comes with BMW's sixth-generation eDrive technology and offers up to 435 miles of EPA range. It will charge quickly, thanks to the 450kW bi-directional charging capability.
With dual 325 horsepower and 245 horsepower rear and front motors, the iX5 60 xDrive puts 570 total horsepower to the ground. That will allow it to accelerate from 0 to 62 MPH in just 4.7 seconds.

The fully-electric iX5 60 eDrive will start at $79,800 (destination charges excluded) and should be on dealer lots by the end of 2026. BMW is also offering the X5 50e plug-in hybrid at $77,500, and the standard ICE X5 40 will start at $69,800.

headline_marked: Meta adds $20 subscription to [[Ray-Ban Meta's Conversation Focus]] feature
headline: Meta adds $20 subscription to Ray-Ban Meta's Conversation Focus feature
summary: Meta introduces a $20/month subscription for advanced features on Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, including extended use of Conversation Focus.
details: Meta has introduced a $20 per month subscription called Meta One Premium, which offers extended use of the Conversation Focus feature on Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses. This feature uses microphones and speakers to help users hear conversations more clearly.

The Conversation Focus feature is restricted to three hours of use per month for non-subscribers, which translates to around six minutes of use per day. Subscribing to Meta One Premium unlocks 15 hours of use per month, or around 30 minutes per day.
The Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses also received other updates, including support for Instagram Instants and WhatsApp voice chats, a battery saver mode, and expanded language support.
It's worth noting that Conversation Focus does not rely on Meta's AI to operate, instead using the smart glasses' hardware and microphones to amplify sound.
